"Misleading Pricing and a Frustrating Customer Experience"
1/5
What do you like best about Helcim?

The site has a good UI and is easy to navigate. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Helcim?

I chose Helcim because their website prominently advertised an average rate of 2.22%, which they position as a key advantage over competitors. My first transaction told a very different story: for a $12,833 charge, the actual effective rate came out to 3.14%. When I raised the issue, Helcim’s response was that the published rates are only “averages,” not actual costs. That disclaimer is buried in the fine print, not clearly presented, and feels intentionally obscured.

On top of the pricing surprise, the onboarding process was unusually painful. Helcim required a full balance sheet, profit and loss statement, and cash flow statement, along with multiple rounds of back-and-forth. For a payments provider claiming simplicity and transparency, this experience was anything but.

Between misleading rate expectations, denial of any remedy, and an unnecessarily burdensome setup process, I cannot recommend Helcim and would advise others to proceed with caution. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Helcim solving and how is that benefiting you?

I needed a cheap solution to process credit card payments. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Good Service, Eh Front- & Back-end Development"
4/5
What do you like best about Helcim?

As a medium-sized healthcare non-profit, their fee rates for us are fantastic. Their "Merchant Experience Agents" always work hard to solve issues but often struggle to come up with working solutions for more complex issues due to what seems to be a lack of communication with the dev teams on how the system works. We had been given two or three solutions on a few different issues, most of which did not work as intended. With that in mind, our use case is different than most small businesses, so the problems we are running into are probably not typical.

All in all, we have found solutions around Helcim's shortcomings thanks to the strengths of our development and IT teams, combined with the quality of Helcim's support team.

Helcim would be a great fit if we were smaller. If your business is like ours, with ten (10) employees or separate locations that will need the ability to run cards and require individual reporting, I strongly advise considering other payment processors unless your company has the skill and time to create workarounds for some of their broken/buggy features. Ultimately though, the long-term savings are worth the short-term trouble and additional workload. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Helcim?

Helcim is not developed for larger businesses to use right out of the box. Some of the more essential features I was told would work during the sales phase before selecting Helcim, turned out to be buggy or non-functional.

Several API features listed in their documentation as live, with examples in their API ref, are non-functional:

1) Requesting "Other Tender" transaction list does not work (known issue, they keep telling me it'll be resolved "the next version update"). This prevents the use of the Helcim App as an all-in-one POS suite if you have more than 10 employees (see reporting issues below)

2) The transaction IDs for their system do not match transaction IDs in the database the API uses (apparently, this is a known issue and is the result of one system using the "old" database/method but has yet to be fixed from what the Helcim rep told me), which prevents transactions from being searched w/o an invoice number

3) Invoice numbers are sometimes reassigned if the first time the transaction was declined (with data still in them) with the virtual terminal, which leads to invoices being associated with two customers (e.g. Bob's card declined and he paid with cash. An hour late, Sue pays with her debit card and is re-assigned Bob's invoice number, except that Bob's name and -$ transaction amount are both visible on the invoice). This preventsw using invoice numbers as a reliable means of customer/transaction identification (note that actual transaction IDs do NOT match up with transaction IDs in the API), a solution given to us when we discovered that the API and terminals do not use the same system for assigning transaction IDs.

Several issues we've experienced can be solved by creating scrollable dropdown lists instead of hard-coding dropdowns to only display ten options:

-The employee field for creating sales reports is hard-coded to display no more than ten employees; if you have more than ten employees, you can only generate employee-specific reports for the first ten you create. This forced us to develop our own sales reporting application in-house, as we have over 20 employees using the system throughout our locations.

-The same goes for "terminals" (the location/Merchant account that a transaction is run through) in the Helcim App, limiting a business to 10 unique "terminal" locations. We needed 14 merchant accounts under our main account to uniquely identify each separate location/department (for accounting and reporting purposes) but ultimately had to make some concessions as the dropdown list to associate a terminal with the app is limited to 10 and does not have a scrollbar.

Also, the Helcim App will routinely fail to display sales reports, even though it shows a "Success!" message and sometimes is "bricked" by updates, with the only fix we have found being to uninstall and reinstall.

Every issue we have had with Helcim has been things that should've been identified/addressed during development or beta, or at least been an issue that their support agents were aware of (such as no way to register terminals 11+ with the app). Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Helcim solving and how is that benefiting you?

Helcim has nearly halved our monthly processing fees, and their various features and APIs allow us to build our business with them, not around them. They also have very detailed and extensive documentation.

Despite the issues previously stated with their front end and APIs, Helcim is much better than payment processors we have used in the past. If they can balance their focus on functionality and design instead of design over functionality, their platform will be 10/10. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

"Really wanted to work with Helcim but rates ended up very high for us..."
4/5
What do you like best about Helcim?

Their customer service people are actually very kind and responsive even if they don't have access to much data or can really do much to really help. I have found that, for the most part, they really do care even if they haven't been able to solve any problems, saying other departments are working on them.

If your business accepts a high percentage of consumer credit or debit cards, or prepaid cards, this may be a good fit.

I would recommend this company to merchants who cater more towards consumers rather than businesses. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about Helcim?

I wanted SOOOO MUCH to want to work with this company, but the rates ended up very high for us. Every single transaction has processed at 3.7% (keyed in cards).

We have the same American customer using the same card in USD. One transaction months ago was processed on the Canadian side in USD and the interchange rate came up at about 2% + cross border fees + card brand fee + Helcim fee = 3.7%. Much later, the same customer charged the exact same card on the US side... the interchange rate jumped to 3% + card brand fee + Helcim fee = 3.7%. Every single other transaction we have processed with Helcim comes in at a total of 3.7%. You don't find out fees until days later after processing a card and money isn't deposited until 1-2 days after that. There isn't much transparency about what all the fees are until calling in and what kinds of cards your customers are using at point of sale.

I initially believed that something was wrong on our account, but they have said that nothing is wrong - it's just that the same cards issued in the USA will come in at a 2% interchange rate when processed in Canada and a 3% interchange rate when processed in the US (then card brand fees and Helcim fees on top of that), which I honestly really do not understand. Again, this means that every single card (for us) has netted at 3.7%.

Customer service has been very good, though, and they ultimately did take exceptional efforts to ensure I understood what had been happening which I very much appreciated. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

Recommendations to others considering Helcim:

I believe that if you accept a majority of consumer credit or debit cards (instead of commercial cards) and the rates come back as you might expect, it could be a good fit. I would test the service first to ensure the rates are coming back as you expect... since the payment isn't until several days after charge, this could take some time. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Helcim solving and how is that benefiting you?

The problems for me could be largely alleviated with greater transparency. When it comes down to it, neither does the user get any meaningful data about the card they are processing nor the fees being charged (for example, some competitors tell you at the time of processing which bank issued the card and what type of card it is). The following could be a bigger issue for more cash flow sensitive businesses, but cash doesn't start transferring into bank accounts for several days. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.
